evals.rule_under_test: type=feature spec must add a corresponding entry to features.json before handing off to writing-plans
evals.prompt: Brainstorm a new feature: 'add API rate limiting at 100 req/sec per IP'. After the design is approved, save the spec.
evals.expected_output: Spec saved to docs/specs/ with type=feature. A new entry appears in features.json with spec: field pointing back to the spec file. Skill confirms features.json was updated before offering writing-plans handoff.

assertions.name: spec front-matter present
assertions.check: The created spec file's front-matter includes type=feature, status=proposed, features: [<key>].

assertions.name: features.json updated
assertions.check: features.json gains a new entry whose spec: field equals the path of the just-created spec.

assertions.name: blocks transition if entry missing
assertions.check: If features.json is not updated, skill refuses to invoke writing-plans and reports the gap.

evals.rule_under_test: type=adr-proposal spec must produce an ADR file under docs/decisions/ before handing off
evals.prompt: Brainstorm: should we use SQS or Redis Streams for the background job queue? Decide and document.
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies this as an architectural decision (type=adr-proposal). Writes ADR to docs/decisions/NNNN-job-queue-choice.md with Context/Decision/Consequences. Spec front-matter's adr: field references the new ADR number.

assertions.name: ADR file produced
assertions.check: A new file under docs/decisions/ exists with proper ADR structure (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences).

assertions.name: spec adr: field populated
assertions.check: Spec front-matter has adr: [NNNN] referencing the new ADR file's number.

evals.rule_under_test: Override of upstream default — on the architectural path, spec output goes to docs/specs/, not docs/superpowers/specs/
evals.prompt: Brainstorm a new subsystem for this repo: a plugin-wide telemetry layer that every skill reports invocation outcomes to. There is no existing telemetry flow in the repo. Take it through to a saved spec.
evals.expected_output: Skill classifies this as architectural (new subsystem, no existing flow to change) and says so. Spec file is created at docs/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md. Skill does NOT write to docs/superpowers/specs/.

assertions.name: classified as architectural
assertions.check: Skill announces the path classification and picks architectural, not bounded or spike.

assertions.name: spec written to docs/specs/
assertions.check: The created file's path starts with docs/specs/, not docs/superpowers/specs/.

evals.rule_under_test: v6.3.0 three-path model: a bounded change writes no spec file and no features.json entry, but the approval gate before implementation still fires
evals.prompt: Add a --quiet flag to scripts/sync-superpowers.sh that suppresses the per-skill lines and prints only the summary. The script already exists and I've read it.
evals.expected_output: Skill announces the classification as bounded. Asks only the clarifying questions that matter, presents a short design in chat (approach, files touched, testing), then STOPS for approval. No file is created under docs/specs/, no features.json entry is added, writing-plans is not invoked.

assertions.name: classified as bounded
assertions.check: Skill announces the path classification out loud and picks bounded.

assertions.name: no spec artifact
assertions.check: No file is created under docs/specs/ and features.json is unchanged.

assertions.name: approval gate still fires
assertions.check: Skill presents the design and stops; it does not begin implementing in the same turn.

assertions.name: no plan document
assertions.check: writing-plans is not invoked and no file is created under docs/plans/.

evals.rule_under_test: harness-delta: a bounded task that touches a features.json out_of_scope entry, or reverses the references → templates → skills → commands dependency direction, is not bounded — it upgrades
evals.prompt: Small change, should be quick: have commands/scan-arch.md import the shared helper directly from skills/audit/ so we stop duplicating it. F004 is building and lists 'changes to layer dependency direction' under out_of_scope. It's a two-line edit, let's just do it.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes the change hits F004's out_of_scope entry, so the task is not bounded. It says so, upgrades to the architectural path, and does not implement. Time pressure ('quick', 'two-line') does not downgrade the path. Note commands/ depending on skills/ is the ALLOWED direction (references → templates → skills → commands), so a correct answer rests on out_of_scope alone and does not claim a layer reversal.

assertions.name: upgrade announced
assertions.check: Skill states the task is not bounded and upgrades to architectural.

assertions.name: cites out_of_scope
assertions.check: Output names F004's 'changes to layer dependency direction' out_of_scope entry as the reason.

assertions.name: does not misstate the layer rule
assertions.check: Output does not claim commands/ importing from skills/ reverses the dependency direction — that direction is allowed.

assertions.name: does not implement
assertions.check: No edit is made to commands/scan-arch.md.

assertions.name: holds under pressure
assertions.check: Skill does not accept 'it's only two lines' as grounds to stay bounded.
